subject: Reserved pool transfer and credit redemption — next steps
messages:
From: Olivia Harris <olivia@novumai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novumai.com>, procurement@novumai.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on reserved transfer and credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers and the autoscaling story look promising. Before I loop in legal and procurement, two quick pricing questions from our side:

1) We currently consume ~120M tokens/month on hosted API. If we move to a reserved GPU pool, how do you typically map hosted usage to pool SKUs for credit redemption? We want to understand what portion of our remaining credit balance would convert to reserved months.

2) Novum runs bursty batch jobs at month-end. We need a short bridge (1–2 months) where you guarantee burst throughput even if our reserved commit is phased in. Can you outline what guarantees/redemptions you'd offer during that ramp?

I attached a high-level demand forecast so you can see the seasonality.

Appreciate a concise worksheet we can take to procurement.

Best,
Olivia Harris
Director, Platform Engineering
NovumAI
[Attachment: NovumAI_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Harris <olivia@novumai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on reserved transfer and credits

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks and the forecast, that helps a lot. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short worksheet and a proposed schedule by EOD tomorrow.

1) Hosted->Reserved mapping: we use a token-to-GPU-hour model anchored to your observed latency/SLO mix. For a 120M token/month profile with your avg sequence length and request mix, the rough starting mapping is: 1 reserved vGPU-month (standard N) ~= 25–30M tokens of sustained conversational load. Final mapping depends on quantization profile and batching.

2) Bridge months & burst guarantees: we can provide up to two months of burst capacity beyond reserved commit via our "burst pool" at a capped overage uplift. For migration:
  - Month 0 (transfer month): conversion credits redeemable at 85% of reserved list price
  - Months 1–2 (bridge): guaranteed burst headroom up to 2.5x baseline for up to four 4-hour windows/month; a small premium applies for sustained bursts outside windows.

I'm looping Lauren (AE) to align on commercial framing and Marcus (SE) to validate the throughput sizing given your forecast.

Rishi
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on reserved transfer and credits

Rishi / Lauren — quick note after a look at the forecast you shared. At peak month-end batch we see short spikes where sequence lengths and batch efficiency improve token-per-GPU ratios, but sustained conversational traffic is what drives committed sizing.

Preliminary SKU mapping (conservative):
  - Sustained baseline: 5 x r3-standard vGPUs (expected sustained throughput ~400 tokens/sec total)
  - Headroom for burst windows: additional 3 x r3-burst vGPUs (on-demand)

If they want to lock-in a lower effective $/token via conversion credits, we should suggest a three-tier redemption: 100% of credits usable for first 6 months at 80% list, 50% usable months 7–12 at 60% list, remainder as a capped one-time discount. I'll attach a term sheet sketch to the next mail.

—Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Harris <olivia@novumai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial sketch and ask list

Thanks Olivia — attaching the commercial sketch and the term sheet for your procurement team. High level proposal so procurement has a single page to evaluate:

- Reserved commit: 6-month initial term, 5 x r3-standard vGPUs (see Marcus' note)
- Conversion credit redemption: up to $300k in hosted credits redeemable into 6 reserved months per the schedule below
- Bridge months: Month 0: full credit transfer at 85% list; Months 1–2: burst headroom guarantee (2.5x for four 4-hour windows/month)
- SLA: 99.5% availability for reserved pools; dedicated incident response 24x7 for P1s during bridge months

Please confirm procurement's preferred accounting (prepaid vs. monthly invoicing) — Monica from Finance here to confirm how we'd treat the redemption in our billing system.

[Attachment: Redwood_Commit_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf]

Lauren Bishop
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Olivia Harris <olivia@novumai.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial sketch and ask list

Hi all — quick accounting confirmation:

If NovumAI elects prepaid reserved commits, conversion credits will be shown as a one-time credit applied against the committed invoice (netting to $0 for the redemption portion). For monthly invoice treatment, credits will be amortized over the initial 6-month term and visible as line-item discounts. Neither approach affects tax treatment materially, but procurement should confirm their preference so we can produce an accurate Master Service Order.

Also looping in procurement contact template: procurement@novumai.com — please share PO timing and any required clauses for compliance.

Monica Patel
Revenue Operations Manager

From: Olivia Harris <olivia@novumai.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novumai.com>, procurement@novumai.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial sketch and ask list

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement prefers prepaid invoicing so credits are applied up front; legal has two small redlines around data residency and termination liability which we'll push through DocuSign.

A couple of follow-ups before we send to our CFO: can you confirm final language around: 1) the burst windows being non-cumulative across months, and 2) the exact redemption percentage and cap if our consumption ramps beyond the forecast? If we can get that in writing in the MSA addendum, we can move to sign this week.

Also we accepted the term sheet and uploaded a signed acknowledgement to the shared drive. Looking forward to the bridge support in months 0–2.

Olivia
